Help & guide

How the Engagement Hub works

A short tour of the things that are easy to miss: what the badges mean, how the conversation with PTAG works, and what lands in your inbox.

Reading your engagements list

Each row carries a badge only when somebody else is waiting on you. It has two states, and they mean different things.

2
Green and gently pulsing — new, unread
Somebody from PTAG has replied and you have not opened the request since. The number is how many comments are waiting, counting only theirs. Your own replies never count towards it.
2
Grey and still — read, but they are still waiting
You have opened it, so the pulse stops. The badge stays because the last word was theirs. It clears the moment you reply.
no badge
Nothing at all — the ball is in their court
Either nobody has commented, or you replied last. There is nothing for you to do.

The counter in the top bar

5
Everything waiting on you, across every request
It only appears when something is actually outstanding, so an empty top bar means you are caught up. Click it to jump straight to just those requests. You can get back to everything with the All chip.

Submitting a request

  1. Tell us about the opportunity. The partner, the idea, and the customer problem behind it. Write the pain points plainly; that section carries real weight.
  2. Add the commercial signals. Addressable market, whether there is an executive sponsor, budget, and certified resources. These feed the score, so guessing high does not help you.
  3. Submit. You get a reference number immediately, an email to confirm, and the request is routed to the right practice automatically.

You can submit from Submit an engagement or the button on the home page.

What happens after you submit

Open any request to see its journey. The step you are on is highlighted, and every step carries a short note about what it means.

Submitted Under Review Need more information In Backlog Planned In Development On Hold Completed

Need more information is the one to watch for. It means PTAG cannot progress your request until you add something, and it is the state most likely to stall if nobody notices it. On Hold is different: PTAG has paused the work on its side, so there is nothing you need to do, and it picks up again when the hold is lifted.

Talking to PTAG

Open any request from My engagements and scroll to Comments. It is a normal two-way thread: what you write there goes to the assessor, and their replies come back to the same place.

  • The whole conversation is visible to you and to PTAG. Internal working notes are kept separate and never appear here.
  • Opening a request marks it as read, which is what stops the badge pulsing.
  • Posting a reply clears the badge completely and brings your new comment into view.

What arrives by email

You do not have to watch the portal. You are emailed when:

  • your request is received, with its reference number
  • it changes state, including when it is accepted or closed
  • PTAG needs more information from you
  • somebody comments on your request

Every one of those emails links straight back to the request.

Finding a specific request

  • Filter by state with the chips at the top of My engagements. Each one shows how many you have in that state.
  • Search by number in the box beside them. Wildcards work, so PTAG00010* finds a range.
  • The same lookup sits on the home page, under your pipeline panel.
  • Every request has a shareable link. Use the copy icon on its row.

Still stuck?

Comment on the request itself — that reaches the assessor who owns it and keeps the question attached to the right context. For anything that is not about a specific request, contact the PTAG team directly.
